winner.name: souji-vault-verify.impl-20.sh
winner.rationale: Only candidate that (a) passes its own selftest and the S63 18/18 battery, (b) refuses the V06 self-referential receipt row that the installed baseline and impl-24 accept as moved-to-obsidian, and (c) reads a complete final ledger row without trailing newline. Its one open defect (rc=1 with no verdict on a mode-000 ledger) is minor and fail-closed in direction (no false-SAFE).

contested_findings.history: case-V6 v1 (14:03) expected NOT-SAFE on a CRLF row truncated to 4 columns. S63 adjudication: the same row with LF endings yields SAFE under the r2 parser (line-ending-dependent verdict = parser accident, not semantics); impl-24/impl-20 strip CR and verify. The fixture was rewritten at 14:07-14:10 and the truncated probe no longer exists; the rewritten V6 expects VERIFIED for both CRLF and LF valid rows, which all three tools satisfy.

s50-vadv E3 (PATH-hijacked sha256sum forging a claim hash) yields VERIFIED/SAFE for all three tools (impl-20, impl-24, r2 baseline) - reproduced by S63 at /tmp/s63/e3. A tool cannot defend against a hostile hasher on its own PATH; recorded as a harness-level caveat, not scored against any candidate.

cli_entry_point_finding.operational_path: read-only sha256sum under the vault path is the only valid vault-side oracle today; official-CLI-based verification is NOT-VERIFIED until the operator runs the app and registers the shim
